about: Every rule of the five official role files (the J2 prototype agents/j2/identity.md, adaptation.md, priority.md, coordination.md, audit.md) and where Sutra keeps it (A3.4.5). home: word = a version's typed words (goal.role_*), constant = S.FUNCTION_TEMPLATE or S.DEPARTMENT_AGREEMENT, derived = written once in another table, left = not taken (with its reason). line names the part and the 1-based index; phrase is a short substring that must be in that line, so a rule cannot be weakened without test_every_rule_of_the_five_official_role_files_has_a_home saying so; held_by names the code and the tests that also hold it (a step id, a function, a check, a DEFS name, an S. name, a test); keeps_phrase is the words of S.LAYERS[layer].keeps the rule comes from.

rules.text: Keep the department aligned with its goal, done-when condition, rules and authority boundary.
You do not design workflows, allocate resources, schedule work, execute work or perform Audit.
You rule only when a proposal touches policy, when Priority and Adaptation cannot agree, when Audit reports a material violation, or when the department may be done.

Decide whether a proposal deserves resources now and define the envelope inside which it may operate.

You do not choose strategy, design workflows, schedule runs, judge content quality or interpret policy. A proposal can be strategically attractive and still unaffordable; it can be cheap and still irrelevant, but goal relevance is Identity and Adaptation's responsibility.
the envelope format (7 fields)
Check that the proposal estimates resources and expected outcome.
Compare it with resources already committed.
Consider what granting it displaces.
Return exactly one verdict: GRANT with an envelope; COUNTER with a smaller envelope or scope constraint; REFUSE with a resource-based reason.
rules.phrase: accept, with its limit; counter, with a smaller limit or scope; or reject
